title: Future forms review
note: BUILT 2026-09-05 (b2/auto), from the 2026-08-29 empty stub. The choice unit B2-PLAN asks for: will · going to · present continuous arrangement · present simple timetable · future continuous · future perfect · the present after a time clause. 30 bank items + a 9-chip sort. A0 is the whole design problem here — Czech has one future, so nothing in the prompt can pick will from going to. Every stem carries the job instead (That looks heavy / Look at those clouds / at four on Thursday / from platform three), the same fix a2_will_going_to took after its 2026-08-29 smoke. C29 timeline on card 0 with now as a centre line, the point, the bar and the deadline to the right of it. B12/B17 Check is a sort into three jobs named by job, sort_cz false (B20), taught form bolded (C37). B3/B6/B4 authored quiz_options everywhere, same lemma, carrying the real errors (will to carry, is going rain, will you working, the museum will open). G4: where both forms would be correct English the chip was dropped, never offered as a wrong. B11 lemma cue on every gap. E7 Use is error-correction, one error per sentence (E2), never an already-correct prompt (E9). C10 a table on every card, C14 card 0 is the unit name, C32 mistakes struck through.

items.en: That looks heavy. I **will** carry it for you.
items.cz: To vypadá těžké. Ponesu ti to.
items.explanation: An offer made at this second → will.
items.explanation_cz: Nabídka v tuhle chvíli → will.

items.en: The phone is ringing — I **will** get it.
items.explanation: You decide while you speak → will.
items.explanation_cz: Rozhoduješ se za řeči → will.

items.en: Perhaps she **will** change her mind.
items.explanation: A guess with nothing to point at → will.
items.explanation_cz: Odhad bez důkazu → will.

items.en: We **are going to** paint the kitchen this summer.
items.explanation: The plan existed before this conversation → going to.
items.explanation_cz: Plán existoval už dřív → going to.

items.en: She **is going to** study medicine after school.
items.explanation: A decision already taken → going to.
items.explanation_cz: Rozhodnutí padlo dřív → going to.

items.en: I **am meeting** the dentist at four on Thursday.
items.cz: Ve čtvrtek ve čtyři mám schůzku u zubaře.
items.explanation: A fixed arrangement with a time → present continuous.
items.explanation_cz: Pevně domluvená schůzka s časem → přítomný průběhový.

items.en: This time tomorrow I **will be sitting** on a beach.
items.cz: Zítra touhle dobou budu sedět na pláži.
items.explanation: It is under way at that future time → will be + -ing.
items.explanation_cz: V ten budoucí čas to zrovna probíhá → will be + -ing.

items.en: At midnight they **will be crossing** the border.
items.explanation: Midnight falls inside the crossing → will be + -ing.
items.explanation_cz: Půlnoc padne doprostřed přejezdu → will be + -ing.

items.en: She **will be working** late all next week.
items.cz: Příští týden bude celý pracovat dlouho do noci.
items.explanation: A whole week of it, seen from now → will be + -ing.
items.explanation_cz: Celý týden, viděno z dneška → will be + -ing.

items.en: That looks heavy. I will carry it for you.
items.cz: To vypadá těžké. Ponesu ti to.
items.gap: That looks heavy. I ____ it for you. (carry)
accepts: That looks heavy. I will carry it for you.
That looks heavy. I'll carry it for you.
items.explanation: You offer as you speak — no plan existed a second ago → **will** carry.
items.explanation_cz: Nabízíš to teď za řeči — před chvílí žádný plán nebyl → **will** carry.
items.wrong: That looks heavy. I will to carry it for you.

items.en: Don't worry, I won't tell anyone.
items.gap: Don't worry, I ____ anyone. (not / tell)
accepts: Don't worry, I won't tell anyone.
Don't worry, I will not tell anyone.
Do not worry, I will not tell anyone.
Do not worry, I won't tell anyone.
Do not worry, I'll not tell anyone.
Don't worry, I'll not tell anyone.
items.explanation: A promise made now → **won't** tell. The negative of will is won't.
items.explanation_cz: Slib daný teď → **won't** tell. Zápor od will je won't.
items.wrong: Don't worry, I not will tell anyone.

items.en: I think prices will rise again next year.
items.cz: Myslím, že ceny příští rok zase porostou.
items.gap: I think prices ____ again next year. (rise)
accepts: I think prices will rise again next year.
items.explanation: **I think** marks an opinion about the future with nothing to point at → will rise.
items.explanation_cz: **I think** značí názor na budoucnost bez důkazu → will rise.
items.wrong: I think prices will to rise again next year.

items.en: The phone is ringing — I will get it.
items.gap: The phone is ringing — I ____ it. (get)
accepts: The phone is ringing — I will get it.
The phone is ringing — I'll get it.
items.explanation: You decide the moment you hear it → **will** get, not a plan.
items.explanation_cz: Rozhoduješ se ve chvíli, kdy to slyšíš → **will** get, ne plán.
items.wrong: The phone is ringing — I will getting it.

items.en: Perhaps she will change her mind.
items.gap: Perhaps she ____ her mind. (change)
accepts: Perhaps she will change her mind.
Perhaps she'll change her mind.
items.explanation: **Perhaps** marks a guess → will change. After will comes the plain verb.
items.explanation_cz: **Perhaps** značí odhad → will change. Po will následuje základní tvar.
items.wrong: Perhaps she will changes her mind.

items.en: Look at those clouds — it is going to pour.
items.cz: Podívej na ty mraky — bude lít.
items.gap: Look at those clouds — it ____. (pour)
accepts: Look at those clouds — it is going to pour.
Look at those clouds — it's going to pour.
items.explanation: The clouds are evidence you can point at → **is going to** pour.
items.explanation_cz: Mraky jsou důkaz, na který můžeš ukázat → **is going to** pour.
items.wrong: Look at those clouds — it is going pour.

items.en: We are going to paint the kitchen this summer.
items.gap: We ____ the kitchen this summer. (paint)
accepts: We are going to paint the kitchen this summer.
We're going to paint the kitchen this summer.
items.explanation: The plan was made before this conversation → **are going to** paint.
items.explanation_cz: Plán vznikl před tímhle rozhovorem → **are going to** paint.
items.wrong: We are going paint the kitchen this summer.

items.en: She is going to study medicine after school.
items.gap: She ____ medicine after school. (study)
accepts: She is going to study medicine after school.
She's going to study medicine after school.
items.explanation: A decision already taken about her life → **is going to** study.
items.explanation_cz: Rozhodnutí už padlo → **is going to** study.
items.wrong: She is going to studies medicine after school.

items.en: Slow down — you are going to hit that post!
items.gap: Slow down — you ____ that post! (hit)
accepts: Slow down — you are going to hit that post!
Slow down — you're going to hit that post!
items.explanation: You can see it coming, right now → **are going to** hit.
items.explanation_cz: Vidíš to přicházet právě teď → **are going to** hit.
items.wrong: Slow down — you are going hit that post!

items.en: They aren't going to move after all.
items.gap: They ____ after all. (not / move)
accepts: They aren't going to move after all.
They are not going to move after all.
They're not going to move after all.
items.explanation: The plan is off — the negative of a plan is **aren't going to** move.
items.explanation_cz: Plán padl — zápor plánu je **aren't going to** move.
items.wrong: They aren't going move after all.

items.en: I am meeting the dentist at four on Thursday.
items.cz: Ve čtvrtek ve čtyři mám schůzku u zubaře.
items.gap: I ____ the dentist at four on Thursday. (meet)
accepts: I am meeting the dentist at four on Thursday.
I'm meeting the dentist at four on Thursday.
items.explanation: A time, a place and another person → a fixed arrangement: **am meeting**.
items.explanation_cz: Čas, místo a druhá osoba → pevná domluva: **am meeting**.
items.wrong: I am meet the dentist at four on Thursday.

items.en: They are flying to Vienna on Saturday morning.
items.cz: V sobotu ráno letí do Vídně.
items.gap: They ____ to Vienna on Saturday morning. (fly)
accepts: They are flying to Vienna on Saturday morning.
They're flying to Vienna on Saturday morning.
items.explanation: Tickets are booked, so it is an arrangement → **are flying**.
items.explanation_cz: Letenky jsou koupené, je to domluvené → **are flying**.
items.wrong: They are fly to Vienna on Saturday morning.

items.en: We are having dinner with Petra tonight.
items.gap: We ____ dinner with Petra tonight. (have)
accepts: We are having dinner with Petra tonight.
We're having dinner with Petra tonight.
items.explanation: Agreed with Petra already → **are having**, the arrangement form.
items.explanation_cz: S Petrou už domluveno → **are having**, tvar pro domluvu.
items.wrong: We are have dinner with Petra tonight.

items.en: What are you doing on Friday evening?
items.gap: What ____ on Friday evening? (you / do)
accepts: What are you doing on Friday evening?
items.explanation: Asking about someone's arrangements → **are you doing**, subject after are.
items.explanation_cz: Ptáš se na domluvené plány → **are you doing**, podmět až za are.
items.wrong: What you are doing on Friday evening?

items.en: The train leaves at 6:40 from platform three.
items.cz: Vlak jede v 6:40 z třetího nástupiště.
items.gap: The train ____ at 6:40 from platform three. (leave)
accepts: The train leaves at 6:40 from platform three.
items.explanation: A timetable the railway set → present simple **leaves**.
items.explanation_cz: Jízdní řád, který sestavily dráhy → přítomný prostý **leaves**.
items.wrong: The train leave at 6:40 from platform three.

items.en: The museum opens at ten on Sundays.
items.cz: Muzeum v neděli otevírá v deset.
items.gap: The museum ____ at ten on Sundays. (open)
accepts: The museum opens at ten on Sundays.
items.explanation: Opening hours belong to the museum, not to you → **opens**.
items.explanation_cz: Otevírací doba patří muzeu, ne tobě → **opens**.
items.wrong: The museum open at ten on Sundays.

items.en: My course starts on the fifth of October.
items.gap: My course ____ on the fifth of October. (start)
accepts: My course starts on the fifth of October.
items.explanation: A date the school fixed → present simple **starts**.
items.explanation_cz: Datum stanovila škola → přítomný prostý **starts**.
items.wrong: My course start on the fifth of October.

items.en: This time tomorrow I will be sitting on a beach.
items.cz: Zítra touhle dobou budu sedět na pláži.
items.gap: This time tomorrow I ____ on a beach. (sit)
accepts: This time tomorrow I will be sitting on a beach.
This time tomorrow I'll be sitting on a beach.
items.explanation: **This time tomorrow** names a moment and the sitting runs through it → will be sitting.
items.explanation_cz: **This time tomorrow** určuje okamžik a sezení jím prochází → will be sitting.
items.wrong: This time tomorrow I will be sit on a beach.

items.en: Don't call at eight — we will be eating.
items.gap: Don't call at eight — we ____. (eat)
accepts: Don't call at eight — we will be eating.
Don't call at eight — we'll be eating.
Do not call at eight — we will be eating.
Do not call at eight — we'll be eating.
items.explanation: Eight o'clock falls inside the meal → **will be** eating, a bar not a dot.
items.explanation_cz: Osmá padne doprostřed jídla → **will be** eating, úsek ne bod.
items.wrong: Don't call at eight — we will be ate.

items.en: She will be working late all next week.
items.cz: Příští týden bude celý pracovat dlouho do noci.
items.gap: She ____ late all next week. (work)
accepts: She will be working late all next week.
She'll be working late all next week.
items.explanation: A stretch of future time, seen from now → **will be** working.
items.explanation_cz: Úsek budoucího času, viděno z dneška → **will be** working.
items.wrong: She will be work late all next week.

items.en: Will you be working when I arrive?
items.gap: ____ when I arrive? (you / work)
accepts: Will you be working when I arrive?
items.explanation: Question order: **Will** + you + be working. My arrival lands inside your work.
items.explanation_cz: Pořádek v otázce: **Will** + you + be working. Můj příchod padne doprostřed práce.
items.wrong: Will you working when I arrive?

items.en: At midnight they will be crossing the border.
items.gap: At midnight they ____ the border. (cross)
accepts: At midnight they will be crossing the border.
At midnight they'll be crossing the border.
items.explanation: Midnight is the moment the crossing is running through → **will be** crossing.
items.explanation_cz: Půlnoc je okamžik, kterým přejezd prochází → **will be** crossing.
items.wrong: At midnight they will be cross the border.

items.en: I won't be coming to the meeting tomorrow.
items.gap: I ____ to the meeting tomorrow. (not / come)
accepts: I won't be coming to the meeting tomorrow.
I will not be coming to the meeting tomorrow.
I'll not be coming to the meeting tomorrow.
items.explanation: Negative of the running form: **won't be** coming, not won't coming.
items.explanation_cz: Zápor průběhového tvaru: **won't be** coming, ne won't coming.
items.wrong: I won't coming to the meeting tomorrow.

items.en: By Friday I will have finished the report.
items.gap: By Friday I ____ the report. (finish)
accepts: By Friday I will have finished the report.
By Friday I'll have finished the report.
items.explanation: **By Friday** is a deadline and the report is done before it → will have finished.
items.explanation_cz: **By Friday** je termín a zpráva je hotová dřív → will have finished.
items.wrong: By Friday I will have finish the report.

items.en: By the time you land, we will have left the airport.
items.cz: Než přistaneš, my už z letiště odjedeme.
items.gap: By the time you land, we ____ the airport. (leave)
accepts: By the time you land, we will have left the airport.
By the time you land, we'll have left the airport.
items.explanation: Your landing is the deadline; our leaving is over before it → **will have left**.
items.explanation_cz: Tvé přistání je termín, náš odjezd je hotový dřív → **will have left**.
items.wrong: By the time you land, we will have leave the airport.

items.en: In August they will have lived here for ten years.
items.cz: V srpnu tu budou bydlet deset let.
items.gap: In August they ____ here for ten years. (live)
accepts: In August they will have lived here for ten years.
In August they'll have lived here for ten years.
items.explanation: Counting up to a future point → **will have lived** for ten years.
items.explanation_cz: Počítáš k budoucímu bodu → **will have lived** for ten years.
items.wrong: In August they will have live here for ten years.

items.en: Will you have read it by Monday?
items.gap: ____ it by Monday? (you / read)
accepts: Will you have read it by Monday?
Will you've read it by Monday?
items.explanation: Question order: **Will** + you + have read. Monday is the deadline.
items.explanation_cz: Pořádek v otázce: **Will** + you + have read. Pondělí je termín.
items.wrong: Will you have readed it by Monday?

items.en: I will call you as soon as I get there.
items.gap: I will call you as soon as I ____ there. (get)
accepts: I will call you as soon as I get there.
I'll call you as soon as I get there.
items.explanation: After **as soon as** English keeps the present, even about the future → get.
items.explanation_cz: Po **as soon as** zůstává angličtina v přítomném čase → get.
items.wrong: I will call you as soon as I will get there.

items.en: We will wait until the rain stops.
items.gap: We will wait until the rain ____. (stop)
accepts: We will wait until the rain stops.
We'll wait until the rain stops.
items.explanation: After **until** the verb stays present → stops. The future is already marked once.
items.explanation_cz: Po **until** zůstává sloveso v přítomném čase → stops. Budoucnost je značená jednou.
items.wrong: We will wait until the rain will stop.

items.en: Send me a message when you arrive.
items.gap: Send me a message when you ____. (arrive)
accepts: Send me a message when you arrive.
items.explanation: A time clause takes the present → **arrive**, however future the meaning is.
items.explanation_cz: Časová věta má přítomný čas → **arrive**, ať je význam jakkoli budoucí.
items.wrong: Send me a message when you will arrive.

bin_captions.Decided as you speak: you choose while you are speaking
bin_captions.Decided before now: the plan or the booking already existed
bin_captions.Running at that moment: in progress at that future time

points: English has no one future tense. It has several forms, and each says something extra.
The form you pick says **how** you know: a decision, a plan, a schedule, a guess.
Czech has one future, so the choice has to come from the situation, not the translation.

rows: you decide as you speak, or you predict
the plan already existed, or you can see it coming
a fixed arrangement, with a time
running through a moment in the future

cards.title: Decided now, or decided already?

rows: you offer or decide on the spot
That looks heavy. I **will** carry it for you.
We are **going to** paint the kitchen this summer.
Slow down — you are **going to** hit that post!

points: Nothing in the Czech picks between these two. The words around the gap do.
**Look at…** and **Slow down…** are evidence you can point at.

cards.title: Arrangements and timetables

rows: I **am meeting** the dentist at four on Thursday.
The train **leaves** at 6:40 from platform three.

points: An arrangement has a time and usually a place — that is the test.
A timetable belongs to a company, a school, a cinema. You cannot change it.

cards.title: Running through a future moment

rows: This time tomorrow I **will be** sitting on a beach.
By Friday I **will have** finished the report.
This time tomorrow · at midnight · by Friday

points: **will be** + -ing is the future twin of *was working* — a bar, not a dot.
**will have** + past participle is the future twin of *had finished*.

cards.title: After when, until, as soon as
cards.title_cz: Po when, until, as soon as

rows: ~~I will call you as soon as I will get there.~~
I will call you as soon as I **get** there.
~~We will wait until the rain will stop.~~
We will wait until the rain **stops**.
~~Send me a message when you will arrive.~~
Send me a message when you **arrive**.

points: English marks the future once. The time clause stays in the present.
Czech marks it twice, which is why this one has to be learned by hand.

cards.title: Common mistakes

rows: ~~I will to carry it for you.~~
~~The museum will open at ten on Sundays.~~
The museum **opens** at ten on Sundays.

points: **will** takes the plain verb — no to.
**going to** keeps its to: going **to** rain.
